meta.scene_summary: We are building an AI-powered future on a power grid that is currently running on thoughts and prayers.

cooking.headline: The Netherlands is breaking up with Microsoft to start its own Linux distro
cooking.summary: The Dutch government is ditching Windows for a custom Linux build, which is the ultimate 'I can fix her' move in the world of enterprise IT. It's a bold strategy that turns a standard office procurement process into a permanent, government-funded side quest.
cooking.plain_english: The government of the Netherlands is transitioning its computer systems from Microsoft Windows and Office to a custom-developed Linux operating system.

cooking.headline: Magnitude wants to optimize your AI agents, because one hallucinating intern wasn't enough
cooking.summary: They've built an inference engine that promises to make agents faster, because apparently, we need our AI to fail at tasks with higher throughput. It's like giving a group project team a faster car so they can drive off the cliff in record time.
cooking.plain_english: Magnitude has released a new software tool designed to improve the performance and speed of AI agents.

cooking.headline: The NRC just gave the green light to a modular nuclear reactor, because apparently we need more power for the GPU farm.
cooking.summary: We are finally getting small. scale nuclear reactors, which is great news if your current energy strategy is 'hope the grid doesn't melt.' It turns out the best way to feed an AI habit is to just build your own private power plant.

cooked.headline: Being the best AI model in the world now has the shelf life of milk
cooked.summary: GPT-6 Sol was replaced by GPT-6.1 Sol in just seven days, making your current prompt engineering feel like a frantic race against a sunset. At this rate, the model will be considered 'legacy' before you even finish reading the documentation.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI released an updated version of its artificial intelligence model just one week after the previous version was launched.

cooked.headline: Tesla is speedrunning the 'take out a massive loan to look profitable' strategy
cooked.summary: Tesla is borrowing $30 billion just as their profitability starts to slide toward zero. It's the corporate equivalent of opening a new credit card to pay off the interest on your last three credit cards.
cooked.plain_english: Tesla has secured 30 billion dollars in credit as the company's profitability declines.

cooked.headline: AI needs to make $6 trillion to pay for its own electricity bill
cooked.summary: The industry needs to generate an absurd $6 trillion annually just to keep the lights on in these massive data centers. It's like buying a Ferrari and then realizing your entire paycheck has to go toward the gas.
cooked.plain_english: The artificial intelligence industry must generate 6 trillion dollars in annual revenue to cover the costs of building and maintaining its data centers.

cooked.headline: ShinyHunters finally learned that 'the cloud' is just someone else's computer, including the FBI's
cooked.summary: The group notorious for leaking massive databases has finally been caught, proving that even elite hackers eventually hit a 404 error in their own opsec. It turns out the only thing harder than exfiltrating terabytes of data is staying anonymous while doing it.
cooked.plain_english: The FBI has arrested the members of the hacking group known as ShinyHunters.

cooked.headline: Data centers are ghosting everyone when asked about their massive water and power consumption.
cooked.summary: Data centers are keeping their utility usage a secret, which is a classic move for someone who knows they're running the shower for three hours a day. It's hard to brag about your carbon-neutral AI goals when you're secretly chugging the entire neighborhood's water supply.
cooked.plain_english: Most data center operators are refusing to disclose how much electricity and water they consume for their operations.

cooked.headline: McDonald's wants an AI to decide if you can afford a Big Mac
cooked.summary: McDonald's is experimenting with AI-driven dynamic pricing to adjust your lunch total in real-time. It's basically the airline ticket model, but for your arteries.
cooked.plain_english: McDonald's is testing artificial intelligence software that automatically changes menu prices based on factors like demand and time of day.

cooked.headline: Insurance companies blame AI for a billion-dollar clerical error
cooked.summary: Blue Cross insurers claim their AI tools accidentally ballooned costs by nearly a billion dollars. It turns out that automating your paperwork is a great way to speedrun a bankruptcy.
cooked.plain_english: Health insurance providers report that the use of automated artificial intelligence systems has resulted in nearly one billion dollars in unexpected additional expenses.
